_description: The gate discipline as data. scripts/trace-report.mjs reads this instead of hardcoding stage names; scripts/verify-push.mjs reads `phase`. Editing THIS file is how the discipline changes; the analyser names no stage. Docs: .cursor/brain/VERIFICATION.md (phases + triggers).
_phaseMeaning: 0 = scaffold (pre-deploy): the push gate runs audit + hooks + version holds + oxlint + format + types + lint + coverage and SKIPS build/web-vitals-chunks/size/e2e — there is no prod boundary to guard before the first deploy. 1 = deployed: the push gate runs the full verify:ci chain. Flip with a one-line commit at the FIRST DEPLOY; GATE_PHASE=full overrides per run (template maintainers push gate machinery with it).

verify.description: hooks -> version holds -> gate env -> oxlint -> format -> tsc -> lint -> coverage -> build -> chunks -> size -> e2e:prod

verify:push.description: phase-aware push gate: phase 0 -> audit + verify:scaffold, phase 1 -> verify:ci

verify:scaffold.description: phase-0 offline gate: hooks -> version holds -> oxlint -> format -> tsc -> lint -> coverage (no build/size/e2e)

verify:measure.description: build + prod-mode look at the result; sanctioned at ANY moment, never a violation

smoke:dev.description: dev-server smoke on its own port

e2e:one.description: one Playwright spec on a free port

docs:check.description: mechanical doc drift: paths, scripts, sentinels, versions, command table, dead docs, agent-memory imports; the push budget vs traced pushes of the same phase (report only)

ci._description: Data for scripts/docs-check.mjs § ciSteps/rulesetContexts. allowedRunSteps lists every `run:` step in a PR-triggered workflow that legitimately runs outside `verify` (install/tooling steps, and the cross-browser/dev-smoke lanes AGENTS.md § the gate documents as CI-only), each with the reason it is not a check that belongs in the gate. rulesetContextAllowlist is for a required status check produced by something other than this repo's own workflows (a third-party GitHub App) — empty today.

allowedRunSteps.reason: pins the npm version the lock file needs; not a check
installs the Playwright browsers the gate needs; not a check
installs OS-level browser dependencies; not a check
the cross-browser job's own build for the geometry spec on Firefox/WebKit; not a check
fails loud on a testMatch that silently selects zero tests; not a lint/type/unit check
the dev-smoke/content-stress lane, deliberately CI-only per AGENTS.md § the gate
the cross-browser lane, deliberately CI-only per AGENTS.md § the gate

docs._description: Data for scripts/docs-check.mjs. sentinels = verbatim fragments of the tier law that may live only in AGENTS.md; versions = doc names -> package names compared with package-lock.json (node -> .nvmrc).
sentinels: never shortened by what the diff touched
Legal at any time, in any lane, never a violation
Parallel lanes never run heavy stages
A skipped stage is printed, never silent

suites._description: Ceilings on the browser suite. It is counted in INVARIANTS, not screens (AGENTS.md § the gate): a route earns a browser test only when it brings an invariant the existing specs do not measure. A suite over its ceiling is a finding, and so is a ceiling more than twice the measurement — that high it flags nothing. Raise a number on a measurement plus a DECISIONS.md line, like a size budget.

commit.description: Husky pre-commit: staged autofix, TDD sibling gate, then repo-wide oxlint/format/tsc. Those run as direct commands, not traced npm scripts, so this moment is declared for completeness.

measure.description: Answering a question only a rendered result can answer. Legal at any time, any lane; has a budget so a slow measurement is still a finding.

push.description: Husky pre-push -> verify:push (phase-aware). Runs unconditionally, never shortened by what the diff touched.
push._budget: NO SECONDS HERE, deliberately, and this matters more in a template than anywhere else. A committed number of seconds describes ONE machine and nothing in the file says which, so every fork inherits a ceiling it may be unable to meet and reads red from its third push - measured ratio between the workstation that set the old numbers and a two-core runner: 5.6x and 10.5x on the same two suites. The gate calibrates a baseline from its OWN first `budgetBaselineMinRuns` runs, per phase, keeps it in the gitignored .gate-budget.json beside the tracer log, and reports drift past `budgetDriftRatio`. The baseline ratchets DOWN by itself when the gate gets faster, the same shape a lint or type baseline uses; it rises only when someone deletes the file, which is the honest way to say this is the new normal. `budgetWindow` keeps one bad day from poisoning p90. A fresh clone starts with no baseline, no red reading, and calibrates to its own hardware.
